text: The AI classification suggests a possible meningioma but the conformal prediction set includes multiple classes, making the result inconclusive and not suitable for clinical action. The finding should be reviewed by a qualified radiologist or specialist physician. Meningiomas arise from the meninges and are the commonest primary brain tumour, often discovered incidentally and may be slow-growing [nci-meningioma]. Presentation depends on location, size, growth rate and histological grade, and two lesions with similar appearance can require very different management [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. A single-slice AI output cannot assess growth rate or grade [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. Clinicians may discuss a detailed neurological examination, dedicated contrast-enhanced MRI with a tumour protocol, specialist review and, where appropriate, histological sampling to inform grading [nci-meningioma][ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. Management options range from observation with serial imaging to surgery or radiation, decisions that require specialist assessment after full clinical evaluation [icom-meningioma-consensus][nci-meningioma]. Follow-up planning, including interval imaging and reassessment if symptoms evolve, should also be determined by the treating team [icom-meningioma-consensus][nci-meningioma].
